subject: ApexCloud: SLA & Order Form redlines — uptime measurement, maintenance windows, evidence request
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie O'Neal <jamie.oneal@apexcloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Sep 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Apex Order Form / SLA redlines + evidence request

Jamie — attaching our initial Order Form redlines and a short summary of the SLA items we want to resolve before legal exchanges the MSA counters. High level asks:

- Confirm uptime measurement methodology (aggregation window, what counts as downtime).
- Propose an agreed maintenance window (frequency + blackout exceptions).
- Clarify service credit formula and monthly cap (we'll propose cap).
- Evidence: SOC 2 report availability and sample uptime reports for last 3 months.

Attachment: Apex_SLA_Redlines_20240929.docx (annotated Order Form)

Proposed quick options for uptime: 99.95% with a monthly credit cap of 20% and stair-step credits (see doc). If Apex prefers 99.9, please confirm the credit schedule you have in mind.

Can we get a call tomorrow morning PT to walk through the redlines? If legal needs to be looped now, please include your counsel.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0184

--
Redwood Inference — High-performance inference for production apps

From: Jamie O'Neal <jamie.oneal@apexcloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@apexcloud.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Sep 2024 11:03:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Apex Order Form / SLA redlines + evidence request

Marcus — thanks for the doc. We're sharing this with procurement and our legal team; attaching our MSA redlines for reference (Apex_MSA_Redlines_20240930.pdf). A few immediate items from us: 

- Apex baseline expectation is 99.9% uptime measured by calendar month.
- Service credits: percentage of monthly fees on a sliding scale (you list a proposed cap).
- Maintenance windows: favor a monthly 4-hour window with 72-hour advance notice; we need to avoid Sunday mornings if possible.

You asked for SOC 2: we can share a SOC 2 Type II repackaged summary after an NDA; otherwise procurement will accept an auditor attestation plus the last three months of aggregated uptime metrics. I'll attach a CSV with our uptime observations.

Questions for Redwood: how do you define "downtime" when there are regional fallback behaviors? If a single region is degraded but traffic fails over to another region, does that count as downtime for the SLA?

Let's schedule 30 minutes tomorrow at 10am PT to align.

Best,
Jamie O'Neal
Head of Procurement, ApexCloud
jamie.oneal@apexcloud.com

Attachment: Apex_MSA_Redlines_20240930.pdf; uptime_report_Q2-Q3_2024.csv

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie O'Neal <jamie.oneal@apexcloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Oct 2024 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Apex Order Form / SLA redlines + evidence request

Jamie — appreciate the quick turnaround and the MSA redlines. Short answers and a counterproposal below (we'll document formally via redline but wanted to capture upfront):

- Measurement: we measure at the account-level across your provisioned capacity. Our proposal: 99.95% measured monthly, where "downtime" = inability to successfully receive and process inference requests to the primary endpoint (HTTP 5xx across all availability zones serving that endpoint). Failover to a different region that maintains request success rates will not be counted as downtime; partial degradation that increases latency beyond an agreed threshold can be treated as "degradation" for metrics but not full downtime unless requests fail.

- Credits: propose a stair-step: 99.95-99.9 -> 10% credit, 99.9-99.0 -> 25% credit, <99.0 -> 50% credit; monthly cap of 20% of monthly fees. This aligns incentives and caps provider liability.

- Maintenance window: prefer weekly rolling 2-hour windows (we can consolidate to a single monthly 4-hour window if Apex requires). Proposed default: Sunday 03:00-05:00 UTC with 48-hour notice for scheduled maintenance and 7-day notice for upgrades that require downtime. Exceptions for agreed blackout periods (e.g., product launch dates) can be negotiated per quarter.

- Evidence: we can provide aggregated uptime reports for the last 3 months (CSV attached earlier). SOC 2 Type II report can be shared under NDA (or via an auditor attestation).

Next steps: I'll loop in our legal (Kimberly) to draft an Order Form redline that tracks these points. If you can confirm your stance on regional failover counting as downtime, we'll prepare the counter redline. Call tomorrow at 10am PT confirmed.

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie O'Neal <jamie.oneal@apexcloud.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Oct 2024 14:22:33 -0700
Subject: Re: Apex Order Form / SLA redlines + evidence request

Jamie / Marcus — Kimberly from Legal. A couple technical/legal clarifications to make the redline easier to accept on both sides: 

1) Measurement window definition: please accept that uptime will be measured across a calendar month using 1-minute sampling of request success rate aggregated to a single monthly percentage. Scheduled maintenance windows and force majeure events will be excluded per Order Form definitions.

2) Definition of Downtime: recommend language: "Downtime means the total cumulative minutes in a month during which the Service is unable to process requests due to Redwood-controlled infrastructure failures, excluding scheduled maintenance, customer misconfiguration, and third-party provider outages beyond Redwood's control." This keeps the scope narrow and defensible.

3) Evidence and audit rights: Redwood will provide quarterly aggregated uptime reports and, upon reasonable request and execution of an appropriate NDA, a SOC 2 Type II summary and copy of the auditor's opinion. We cannot provide raw system logs to customers; instead we can provide an agreed evidence bundle (aggregated uptime CSV + incident timeline PDF).

Attachment: internal_redline_MSA_notes_20241001.pdf (for internal reference)

Please review the above language and confirm if Apex legal would accept the sampling granularity and the evidence bundle approach rather than raw logs. If Apex requires broader audit rights, we'll need to scope that in the Order Form with indemnities.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

From: Jamie O'Neal <jamie.oneal@apexcloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@apexcloud.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Oct 2024 10:10:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Apex Order Form / SLA redlines + evidence request

Kimberly — thanks for the clarity. A few follow-ups from Apex legal/procurement side: 

- Sampling: 1-minute sampling is acceptable, but Apex wants an explicit statement that aggregation uses weighted availability across regions when multi-region endpoints are configured.

- Evidence: we can accept the evidence bundle plus SOC 2 summary, but procurement will also ask for uptime reports for the last 6 months if available (we need to understand seasonality). Can you provide last 6 months of aggregated reports (CSV) and a short incident timeline for any P1 events?

- Credits: Apex legal is reluctant about a 20% cap; will propose a higher cap for critical enterprise customers. Can you share the rationale behind 20% (benchmarks or examples)? 

- Maintenance: Apex still prefers monthly 4-hour windows; the exact day can be flexible but they require at least 72-hour notice and a rollback plan for any deployment that could impact availability.

We'll review the updated redline once Redwood legal sends it. If you can post the redline to DocuSign or shared Drive, we can start collaborative edits.

Thanks,
Jamie

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie O'Neal <jamie.oneal@apexcloud.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Oct 2024 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Apex Order Form / SLA redlines + evidence request

Jamie — great feedback. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Regional weighting: agreed — we'll include explicit language that availability for multi-region endpoints will be weighted by configured traffic percentages and that failover behavior will be documented in the Order Form.

- Evidence: we'll produce 6 months of aggregated uptime CSV + incident timeline for P1 events within 3 business days. The SOC 2 summary will be made available after a standard confidentiality addendum; I'll have Contracts send the NDA link today.

- Credit cap rationale: the 20% cap is meant to strike a balance between meaningful customer compensation and protecting both parties from disproportional liability on a single monthly bill. We can accept a higher cap for Apex enterprise accounts subject to onboarding/commit sizing — propose we table the cap for the enterprise addendum and keep 20% in the base Order Form. We will document enterprise exceptions in the Order Form.

- Maintenance: we'll default to a monthly 4-hour window to match your preference and will include a 72-hour notice requirement and rollback plan language.

Action items: 
1) Redwood Legal (Kimberly) to post the redline bundle to the shared Drive and DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/documents/3A5F2 
2) Redwood Contracts to send confidentiality addendum for SOC 2 access.
3) Marcus to upload 6 months of aggregated uptime CSV to shared Drive for Apex review.

I'll follow up once docs are posted. Appreciate the quick cycle.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
